$comment: Hand-edited properties; geometry rebuilt from trace.json by make past (decision 12).

properties.name: The Western Pacific's mole, to Chestnut Junction
properties.notes: About 11,000 feet long, between the Southern Pacific's mole and the estuary's mouth (Tribune, 1910). Its passenger slips went out of use in 1918-20 and for good in 1933; when the track itself went isn't sourced.
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS San Francisco 1:62,500 (1915) (10 hand-read points); the sheet corrected by a shift on 3 control points (Yerba Buena Island on the 1949 Oakland West sheet; +74 m E, +213 m N, RMS 44.8 m). The line the 1915 sheet labels Western Pacific, from its ferry slips at the end of the mole, south of the Southern Pacific's, along the mole and across the estuary's mouth to Chestnut Junction at First and Chestnut Sts.

properties.name: Ferry, the Western Pacific mole to the Ferry Building
properties.notes: Two slips at the Ferry Building, at the foot of Market St (Tribune, 1910).
properties.geometry_method: The shortest path over today's water from -122.32979,37.80006 to The Embarcadero/Market Street (5809 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 land and water), kept off the shore: the sources give the terminals, not the course.

properties.name: Oakland, Chestnut Junction by Third St to Fruitvale
properties.notes: Double track along Third St, with crossings at Webster St, Broadway and Washington St (Tribune, 1909); the depot was at Third and Washington Sts. The Southern Pacific's track crossed at Magnolia Tower, First and Chestnut Sts, the WP's Chestnut Junction.
properties.geometry_method: Traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (5 hand-read points); then along today's 3rd Street centerline from -122.28924,37.80107 to Oak Street (2087 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) (13 hand-read points); then traced by eye from USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949) (9 hand-read points); then OpenHistoricalMap way 200236876 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), cut to -122.21967,37.76968; checked on USGS Oakland West 1:24,000 (1949) and USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949). From Chestnut Junction up to Third St, and along Third St, where the 1909 Tribune puts its double track and the 1949 sheets draw it, past the depot at Washington St to Oak St; then across the Lake Merritt channel and the yard at Fifth Ave, the northern tracks of the pair beside the Southern Pacific's, as the 1949 sheets label them; then OpenHistoricalMap's way from the 1915 sheet to today's Oakland Subdivision at Fruitvale.

properties.name: Fruitvale to Niles, by San Leandro and Hayward

sources.note: Fruitvale, Melrose, Elmhurst, San Leandro, Hayward, Decoto and Niles.

properties.notes: Still in place, as the Union Pacific's Oakland Subdivision.
properties.geometry_method: Along OpenStreetMap's UP Oakland Subdivision from -122.21967,37.76968 to -121.96810,37.57450 (32613 m; Overture 2026-09-23.1 rail); checked on USGS Oakland East 1:24,000 (1949), USGS San Leandro 1:24,000 (1948), USGS Hayward 1:62,500 (1915) and USGS Niles 1:24,000 (1953). Today's Oakland Subdivision, the Western Pacific's line, from Fruitvale by Melrose, Elmhurst, San Leandro, Hayward and Decoto to Niles, where ACE's track joins it.

properties.name: Niles Junction by Irvington to Warm Springs

sources.note: The first train over the new line, from Oakland to San José, on August 23, 1922.

properties.notes: The Western Pacific's San José branch; Irvington and Warm Springs were on it (Sawyer, 1922, read in the scan's text only).
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 200451853 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS Pleasanton CA 1941 topographic map; checked on USGS Niles 1:24,000 (1953) and USGS Milpitas 1:24,000 (1953). The San José branch from Niles Junction, on the main line just east of Niles, south by Irvington to Warm Springs, beside the Southern Pacific; the 1953 Niles sheet labels it Western Pacific and draws it where the way runs.

properties.name: Warm Springs by Milpitas and Berryessa to East San José

sources.note: The first train over the new line, from Oakland to San José, on August 23, 1922.

properties.notes: Berryessa was a flag stop in 1931 (CRC D23837). BART's Silicon Valley extension runs on this right of way today.
properties.geometry_method: OpenHistoricalMap way 198748683 (CC0, as of 2026-10-16), which OHM's mappers drew from USGS San Jose CA 1943 topographic map; checked on USGS Milpitas 1:24,000 (1953) and USGS San Jose 1:62,500 (1943). From Warm Springs by Milpitas and Berryessa to the edge of east San José, where the way tagged Western Pacific ends; the 1943 San Jose sheet labels the line. BART's Silicon Valley extension runs on this right of way today. The branch's East San José depot isn't placed by any source here.
